rq_ship.prompt: What did you ship this quarter?

answers.text: Two features, one fix. Notes attached.
Lots of small things. Hard to list.
I was busy. Very, very busy.

rq_credit.prompt: A teammate says the demo was mostly theirs.

answers.text: True in part. I will name who did what.
We worked on it together.
Ask anyone. Actually, do not ask anyone.

rq_weak.prompt: What is one thing you could improve?

answers.text: I wait too long to ask for help.
I care too much. It's a problem.
Nothing. Next question.

rq_feedback.prompt: Last month I said your changes were too big.

answers.text: I split them now. Reviews are faster.
I'll try to keep them smaller.
They're big because the work is big.

rq_outage.prompt: You were on call during the outage.

answers.text: I escalated early and wrote it up.
I fixed it. Long night.
What outage?

rq_goal.prompt: Where do you want to be in a year?

answers.text: Owning a project from start to finish.
Here. Maybe with a nicer chair.
Your job. No offense.
I flagged the risk on day 3, in writing.
It was bigger than we thought.
Deadlines are a social construct.

rq_help.prompt: A teammate says you rarely help with reviews.

answers.text: Fair. I will block time for it daily.
I help when I have time.
Tell them to read faster.

rq_curve.prompt: Why should I rate you above the curve?

answers.text: Here are my results and who they helped.
I work hard and I'm nice.
Because I said so. In writing. To HR.
I had a conflict and sent notes ahead.
I thought it was optional.
I attended in spirit.

rq_scope.prompt: The client wants one more small feature.

answers.text: I will size it and say what moves.
Sure, we'll fit it in.
Yes. Also a pony. Also my weekend.

rq_docs.prompt: Nobody can find your design doc.

answers.text: It's linked in the ticket now. Sorry.
It's somewhere. I think.
Docs are for people with time.
